title: U.S. House · Indiana's 8th District
area: Southwestern Indiana, including Evansville, Vincennes, and Jasper.

context.text: Incumbent Mark Messmer ran unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Mary Allen won the Democratic primary with 66.7% of the vote over three challengers.

summary.text: Mark Messmer is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 8th Congressional District. A mechanical engineer and small business owner from Jasper, he served in the Indiana House and Senate, including as Senate majority leader, before winning the open seat in 2024. His campaign materials cite endorsements from President Donald Trump and Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America.

background.text: Born September 21, 1962, in Jasper, Indiana, and raised in Southern Indiana.
Earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Purdue University (1985).
Worked as a project engineer with John Brown Engineering and Dow Chemical, and is co-owner of Messmer Mechanical; his House biography says he and his wife, Kim, are small business owners.

Served on the Holy Family School Board in Jasper from 2001 to 2004, including as president in 2003-2004, and has been a parish council member and music minister at Holy Family Catholic Church, according to his House biography.

Served in the Indiana House of Representatives (District 63) from 2008 to 2014, then in the Indiana Senate (District 48) from 2014 until he resigned in September 2024 to focus on his congressional campaign.
In the Indiana Senate, served as majority leader from 2018 to 2022 and chaired the Senate Environmental Affairs Committee and the Joint Rules Committee.
Won the May 2024 Republican primary for the open 8th District seat (38.5% to former U.S. Rep. John Hostettler's 19.7%) and the November general election, succeeding retiring Rep. Larry Bucshon.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry), the Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Has introduced the Heat Workforce Standards Act, which would repeal a Biden-administration OSHA workplace heat-safety rule, according to Lakeshore Public Media.
Received the presidential endorsement of Donald Trump in 2026.

priorities.text: Describes himself as pro-life and credits his Indiana statehouse work with the state's abortion restrictions since Roe v. Wade was overturned.
priorities.quote: Thanks to my work in the Statehouse, Indiana now has the most protective Pro-Life legislation in the nation since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

priorities.text: Supports securing the southern border and ending birthright citizenship for people in the country illegally.
priorities.quote: We need to secure the southern border and deport the illegal immigrants that Joe Biden has allowed to flood into our country. We need to end birthright citizenship for people that are here illegally.

priorities.text: Supports a cryptocurrency regulatory overhaul that promotes blockchain innovation and opposes central bank digital currencies.

positions.summary: Credits his Statehouse work with Indiana's pro-life legislation and says he will continue to defend the unborn and work to expand adoption and other abortion alternatives.
positions.quote: Thanks to my work in the Statehouse, Indiana now has the most protective Pro-Life legislation in the nation since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border, deporting people in the country illegally, and ending birthright citizenship for undocumented immigrants; as an Indiana state senator voted for bills allowing law enforcement to detain undocumented immigrants who committed felonies, banning sanctuary universities and cities, and requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.
positions.quote: I have voted to allow law enforcement to detain illegal aliens that have committed a felony until immigration officials can take them into custody (SEA590). I voted to ban sanctuary universities (SEA243). I co-authored a ban on sanctuary cities (SEA181), and voted to require proof of citizenship to register to vote (HEA1264).

record.text: As an Indiana state senator, voted for SEA 590 allowing law enforcement to detain undocumented immigrants who committed felonies until immigration officials take custody.
As an Indiana state senator, voted for SEA 243 banning sanctuary universities and co-authored SEA 181 banning sanctuary cities.
As an Indiana state senator, voted for HEA 1264 requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.
Introduced a bill on Ready Reserve Force modernization in the U.S. House.
Announced passage of the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act in the House of Representatives.

candidates.name: Mary Allen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 66.7% of the vote.

summary.text: Mary Allen is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 8th Congressional District. She is an Evansville small business owner, Army Reserve veteran and at-large member and vice president of the Evansville City Council, running on affordability, health care and accountability.

background.text: Lives in Evansville, Indiana. She says she grew up in a working-class family, with a father who was a Teamster and truck driver, and has lived in Indiana for a little over 30 years with her husband, Greg.
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve.

In a WNIN interview, she said she worked in health care for 15 years and alongside her husband in a nonprofit ministry for almost a decade, and has owned small businesses for 15 years, most recently a retail store on Main Street in Evansville. Ballotpedia lists her as owner of Sixth and Zero and affiliated with Virginia Street Properties.
At-large member of the Evansville City Council, where she has also served as council vice president; she describes herself as a Rotary member.
Has served on the Vanderburgh County Solid Waste Board and the Evansville Metropolitan Planning Organization, and chaired the Enterprise Zone.
Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 66.7% of the vote over three candidates; she was endorsed by the district Democratic party, according to WNIN.
Describes herself as a mother and grandmother of two.

priorities.text: Says families are struggling with an affordability crisis: rent, groceries, and healthcare costs outpacing wages, and supports fair markets and breaking up corporate monopolies she says are squeezing workers and farmers.
priorities.quote: We are in an affordability crisis. Families earning minimum wage need over full-time hours to afford a modest apartment... Corporate monopolies have rigged the system.

priorities.text: Says healthcare should be a right, citing rising insurance premiums, drug costs, and surprise medical bills.
priorities.quote: She believes accessible and affordable healthcare is a right, not a privilege.

priorities.text: Wants Congress to listen more to constituents' concerns on education, immigration, healthcare, and affordability rather than repeating national talking points.

positions.summary: Says on her campaign site that healthcare is a human right and that universal healthcare lowers costs, and lists protecting and expanding Medicaid and Medicare among her healthcare priorities.
positions.quote: Protecting and expanding Medicaid and Medicare.

positions.summary: Lists ensuring the ultra-wealthy and corporations pay their fair share in taxes among her tax priorities.
positions.quote: Ensuring the ultra-wealthy and corporations pay their fair share in taxes.

positions.summary: Lists ending military support to Israel among her foreign policy priorities.
positions.quote: Ending military support to Israel to align foreign aid with human rights and international law.

statements.quote: Supporting the War Powers Resolution to end the unpopular, illegal war in Iran.
statements.context: On her campaign site, under "Foreign Policy"

statements.quote: Lower energy costs, diversify our energy supply, and create thousands of local, clean-energy jobs by investing in wind, solar, and modern grid infrastructure.
statements.context: On her campaign site, under "Environment and Energy"

statements.quote: Ensuring no family pays more than 7% of their income for childcare.
statements.context: On her campaign site, under "Childcare & Working Families"

statements.quote: Ensuring your paycheck covers your basic needs through a national minimum wage tied to inflation.
statements.context: On her campaign site, under "Good Jobs"

statements.quote: Making your groceries more affordable by removing tariffs on food and other essentials and stopping corporate price hikes.
Making homeownership more affordable through investments that build homes for working families, not luxury condos.
We cannot continue to treat hardworking families as criminals, rounding people up and denying them due process.
statements.context: On her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, quoting her campaign website; she also says "I believe in strong borders."

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from her campaign priorities page and Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Her rent comment ("expanding affordable housing programs") is not recorded as a rent regulation position. No statements found on guns, abortion, police funding or school choice.

summary.text: James Burke is an independent who sought Indiana's 8th Congressional District seat and describes himself as a Terre Haute native running a social-media-only campaign without fundraising. Ballotpedia states he will not appear on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Terre Haute South High School, completed a carpenter's apprenticeship, and attended Western Governors University.

priorities.text: Supports raising taxes on companies with large profits to fund universal healthcare, and says big money should not have a place in elections.
priorities.quote: I believe if the billionaires pay their far share we can have universal health care... I believe big money has no place in our elections and both houses of congress need to get back to working with the people.

priorities.text: Supports LGBTQ+ rights, marriage equality, and describes himself as pro-choice and pro-union.

positions.summary: Supports taxing highly profitable companies to fund universal healthcare and points to high ambulance and medical costs as a policy priority.
positions.quote: The absorbent price of Healthcare, $4000 for a 5 minute ambulance ride, having to file bankruptcy or lose everything you've worked for because you got sick.

positions.summary: Supports taxing highly profitable corporations more heavily, saying large companies should either pay a living wage or be taxed.
positions.quote: there's no reason a company making 100 billion net profit should have any employee needing assistance.
